stops.name: Westerkerk
stops.en: Built in 1620-1631, located on Westermarkt near the Anne Frank House. You can climb the tower (with a guide only) every half hour, M-Sa €6. The tower is also open in the winter by group appointment (maximum 10 people) for €70/hr. In good weather you can see all of Amsterdam, and as far as the coast. Free organ concert held every Friday at 13:00.
stops.lc: Hier ligt een uniek stedelijk park op het voormalige Westergasfabriekterrein waar veel culturele activiteiten plaatsvinden. Wandelend kom je op veel plaatsen beeldende kunst, historische plekken en bijzondere architectuur tegen.

stops.name: Nieuwe Kerk
stops.en: Used for royal coronations, including the crowning of King Willem-Alexander in 2013, and royal weddings, including his wedding to princess Máxima in 2002. The church is no longer used for services but is now a popular exhibition space. Admissions are limited: by tickets online to reserve a space.
stops.lc: Gelegen naast het Koninklijk Paleis. Hier zijn regelmatig wisselende tentoonstellingen te zien. Ook wordt deze kerk gebruikt voor speciale gelegenheden (zoals de kroning van het staatshoofd).

stops.name: Vondelpark
stops.en: The only large park that is close to the Binnenstad, and definitely the most popular one. Especially in the summer, it is lively and crowded, many locals sit on the grass and enjoy a cold beer or wine. It's a lovely place to just hang out, sit in the sun and meet the locals. Open-air theaters are running in the summer on Friday evenings, Saturdays and Sundays.
stops.lc: De long van Amsterdam met onder meer ook het Filmmuseum.

stops.name: Oude Kerk
stops.en: The oldest of the five main churches in the historic centre, and probably the oldest building in Amsterdam. It is right in the heart of the Red Light District. You can climb the tower from April to September on Saturday and Sunday, every half-hour. Also open in the winter by group appointment (maximum 10 people) cost €70 per hour. E-mail for more information.
stops.lc: Het oudste gebouw van de stad, met exposities en concerten.

stops.name: Rijksmuseum
stops.en: The largest and most prestigious museum for art and history in the Netherlands: works by Vermeer, Rembrandt, and other Dutch masters. Its garden has a curious collection of architecture and has free entrance during museum opening times. Recommend getting there early to avoid long queues and crowds, then head first for the second floor to see the Rembrandt classics and others such as Avercamp's Win
stops.lc: Een verplicht nummer voor een dagje Amsterdam. Hier hangt De Nachtwacht, maar ook andere schilderijen van Rembrandt, Vermeer, Steen, Hals etc. Momenteel een grote verbouwing gaande maar na de verbouwing ook weer poppenkabinet, porselein en vaderlandse historie afdelingen te bewonderen. Het museum ondervindt momenteel een grote verbouwing zodat een gedeelte gesloten is.

stops.name: Anne Frank House
stops.en: The house where the Jewish girl Anne Frank wrote her diary while hiding with her family from the Nazis. One must buy tickets online, only 20% are issued on the same day so buy them in advance. During high season tickets can be sold out a month in advance. To be safe, you should book 6 weeks in advance. Museumkaart is valid, I Amsterdam Card is not valid.
stops.lc: Het museum vertelt het verhaal van het Joodse meisje Anne Frank dat hier ondergedoken zat in de 2e Wereldoorlog, haar wereldberoemde dagboek schreef en na verraad gedeporteerd werd naar een concentratiekamp dat zij niet overleefd heeft. Reserveer kaarten van te voren via hun site als je niet uren in de rij wilt staan.

stops.name: Concertgebouw
stops.lc: Reserveren op dit nummer 7 dagen per week van 10-17 uur. Het Concertgebouw is een van de beroemdste muziekcentra ter wereld met een welhaast ongeëvenaarde akoestiek. Ca. 700 producties per jaar. Met in de zomermaanden de relatief zeer goedkope maar kwalitatief uitstekende Robeco zomerconcerten, en vrijwel iedere woensdag middag om 12:30 uur gratis lunch concerten in de vorm van repetities van het

stops.name: Stedelijk Museum Amsterdam
stops.en: The Stedelijk Museum is the municipal museum of modern art. It has a long history, as it first opened in 1874 and has been at its current location since 1895. It was reopened in 2012 after a renovation that took four years: the new building is now locally referred to as the "bath tub" due to its unique shape. The "bath tub" will host newly acquired film and video expositions, while the highlights
stops.lc: Het Stedelijk Museum is de plek waar iedereen 365 dagen per jaar moderne en hedendaagse kunst en vormgeving kan ontdekken en beleven.

stops.name: Royal Palace of Amsterdam
stops.en: The Royal Palace is one of the three official palaces of the Netherlands. It is at the disposal of King Willem-Alexander by the Act of Parliament. It was built in 1651 as the city hall of Amsterdam, in a period known as the Dutch Golden Age. Many school children learn that because of the swampy soil, it was built on no less than 13,569 wooden poles. In 1795, the French Empire of Napoleon Bonaparte

stops.name: Rembrandt House Museum
stops.en: This public square features a larger-than-life statue of Rembrandt on a pedestal.

stops.name: Homomonument
stops.en: The Homomonument is a memorial to gays and lesbians murdered in World War II, a call for vigilance against homophobia, and an inspiration for gays and lesbians the world over. It consists of three equilateral triangles made of pink granite that are connected by an inlaid band of pink bricks. These three triangles represent the past, present and future.

stops.name: Magere Brug
stops.en: The Magere Brug, literally "Skinny Bridge", is a bridge that spans the Amstel River and connects the Kerkstraat with the Nieuwe Kerkstraat. It's an iconic bridge that consists of nine arches and a drawbridge that is still operated by hand. The current bridge is made of white-painted wood, but it has been rebuilt several times and historically it has also been in concrete. The first bridge here was

stops.name: Portuguese Synagogue
stops.en: The most prominent synagogue of the city centre, the Esnoga dates back from 1675 and is built in an austere Classicist style. In 1492, Spain expelled its Jewish population as part of the Inquisition, and many fled to Portugal. One hundred years later, their descendants migrated to Amsterdam for its religious freedom. This happened at a time when the Dutch provinces were fighting for independence a

stops.name: Our Lord in the Attic Museum
stops.local: Museum Ons' Lieve Heer op Solder
stops.en: One of the oldest museums in Amsterdam, this is a Catholic church stuffed into the upper stories of a house built in 1663, when Catholics were persecuted and had to disguise their churches. It's amazing to see how they fit worshippers, an organ, and an altar into such a narrow place.
stops.lc: Te bezichten grachtenpand met op zolder een voormalige katholieke schuilkerk.

stops.name: National Monument on Dam Square
stops.en: A large spire that functions as a memorial for the victims of World War II. It was designed by architect J.J.P. Oud and revealed on 4 May 1956. Every 4 May, at the Remembrance of the Dead, a ceremony is held here to commemorate all civilians and members of the Dutch armed forces that died in World War II and later armed conflicts.

stops.name: Museum of the Canals,  Amsterdam
stops.en: Het Grachtenhuis is the gateway to the world-famous Canal District. Het Grachtenhuis tells the fascinating story of how Amsterdam's Canal District was created by a multi-media exhibition.
stops.lc: Interactief en multimediaal museum over de ontstaansgeschiedenis van de 17e-eeuwse Amsterdamse grachtengordel.

stops.name: Van Gogh Museum
stops.en: This museum is dedicated to Vincent van Gogh, a late 19th-century Post-Impressionist Dutch painter. Tickets are available online only, and can be booked out weeks in advance during busy periods. In the museum are many, but not all, of Van Gogh's works. The museum contains some famous paintings like Sunflowers and Potato Eaters, but lacks others such as Starry Night. Also, there are selected works

stops.name: Amsterdam Central station
stops.en: This beautiful building is an attraction in itself, so if you did not arrive in Amsterdam by train, it is well worth making a special trip to look at the station's facade. The station was built between 1881 and 1889 on three artificial islands. It was designed by Pierre Cuypers who also designed the Rijksmuseum in a similar neo-late-Gothic/Renaissance style. At the time, the project was highly con

stops.name: Natura Artis Magistra
stops.en: An entry ticket for Artis also provides admission to the Planetarium, the Aquarium and the Zoological Museum. Artis is also a botanical garden, with plants and trees gathered from all over the world, just like the animal species. Don't miss the Artis ZOOmeravonden.

stops.name: Wereldmuseum Amsterdam
stops.en: Ethnographic and cultural museum about Africa, Asia and South America. Includes an excellent cafe which sells food from around the world. Tickets are discounted if reserved online.

stops.name: NEMO Science Center
stops.lc: Een interactief wetenschapsmuseum. Zeker een aanrader als je met kinderen Amsterdam komt bezoeken. In de schoolvakanties zijn er vaak activiteiten.

stops.name: Museumplein
stops.en: Not exactly a park, but a large grassed open space. Around its edges are the Rijksmuseum, the Van Gogh Museum, the Stedelijk Museum and the Concertgebouw. On a sunny summer day, many locals chill on the grass lawn on top of the Albert Heijn supermarket.

stops.name: Amsterdam Museum
stops.en: A museum about the history of Amsterdam.

stops.name: H'Art Museum
stops.en: Founded as an outpost of the Hermitage in St Petersburg, ties were severed with the parent institution following Russia's war in Ukraine. After a hasty rebrand, the H'ART museum reopened in April 2022 with a focus on Dutch heritage in Amsterdam.

stops.name: Hortus Botanicus Amsterdam
stops.en: The Amsterdam Botanical Gardens — 'Hortus' as they are called by locals — used to be the Botanic Garden of the University of Amsterdam. It is one of the oldest botanical gardens in the world. Nowadays it is an independent organisation. The collection of the garden consists of more than 6,000 species. The garden regularly holds extra exhibitions and music performances.

stops.name: Zuiderkerk
stops.en: Built in 1603-1611. Located on Zuiderkerkhof ("Southern Graveyard"). Now an information centre on housing and planning. You can visit the tower from April to September Monday to Saturday (with guide only) every half-hour, cost €6. Also open in the winter by group appointment (maximum 15 people) cost €70 per hr. E-mail for more information.

stops.name: Cat Cabinet
stops.en: A cat museum. Housed in a beautiful restored palatial home in an upscale area street - very Masterpiece Theater. It was opened by the homeowner after his favourite cat died... and he still lives in the home. Lots of cat-related art, and two real felines. The exhibition is spread across the first floor of the house.

stops.name: Beurs van Berlage
stops.en: Take a guided tour and check out the view from the top of the old stock exchange tower. It was built in 1903 (by Hendrik Petrus Berlage) and is considered the beginning of modern Dutch architecture. Costs €3.50, located on Beursplein near Dam Square.

stops.name: Heineken Experience
stops.en: Do not expect a beer museum, but rather to be flooded with Heineken advertisements.
stops.lc: De voormalige brouwerij is nu geopend als museum.

stops.name: Begijnhof
stops.en: The Begijnhof is a late medieval enclosed courtyard with the houses of beguines (Roman Catholic women living in a semi-religious community). It is a very picturesque group of historic buildings, mostly private dwellings. House number 34 is the oldest home in Amsterdam. The courtyard also has a Reformed Church and a hidden Catholic chapel. Surprisingly, it feels like a serene oasis as it is surroun

stops.name: Museum Van Loon
stops.en: 17th century house with interior restored with furnishings to how it looked in the 18th century. Also interesting to see a garden you would not normally see from the streets.

stops.name: Sarphatipark
stops.en: Situated in De Pijp, this is a place where people sunbathe and have picnics in the summer.
stops.lc: Het lieflijke park midden in de Pijp om even bij te komen van alle hectiek van de buurt.

stops.name: De Otter
stops.en: A restored and functioning sawmill, opposite Buyskade, west of the Jordaan.

stops.name: De Gooyer
stops.en: It's the only windmill (1814, restored) in the centre of Amsterdam, and the closest one that's open to visitors.

stops.name: Huis met de Kabouters
stops.en: Named after two gnomes decorating its facade, this building is in a mix of Gothic and Renaissance Revival and includes gargoyles and narrow lancet windows. Built in 1884, it became a rijksmonument in 1984.

stops.name: De 1100 Roe
stops.en: In the Ookmeer sports fields along Ma Braunpad.

stops.name: De 1200 Roe
stops.en: Near Seineweg.

stops.name: De Bloem
stops.en: at Nieuwpoortkade.

stops.name: Molen van Sloten
stops.en: In Zuid, the only one open for visitors

stops.name: D'Admiraal
stops.en: Windmill on the bank of the Noordhollands Kanaal in the north, ferry from Central Station.

stops.name: Frankendael
stops.en: Frankendael is a house built in 1733 in Watergraafsmeer. The house is surrounded by a pleasant park. Take tram 9, get off at the stop "Hugo de Vrieslaan".

stops.name: Johan Cruyff Arena
stops.en: The Johan Cruijff ArenA, built from 1993 to 1996, has a capacity of 55,865 seats during sports matches. It's the home ground of AFC Ajax, who play in the Eredivisie, the top tier of football in the Netherlands; the Dutch national team also play here. The arena can hold up to 71,000 people during concerts and regularly holds popular music events. Ajax offers multiple daily tours through the stadium

stops.name: Royal Netherlands Academy of Arts and Sciences
El Al Flight 1862
stops.en: Protected monument to the original 1960s urban vision of the modernist Bijlmermeer expansion of Amsterdam. It consists of the high-rise flats Gooioord, Groeneveen, Grubbehoeve, Kikkenstein, Kleiburg and Kruitberg, the brutalist metro viaduct running between them and the parks they are all located in. You can get a tour of parts of the Grubbehoeve flat by appointment, but if the weather's good just

stops.name: Skull of a Skeleton with Burning Cigarette
stops.local: Kop van een skelet met brandende sigaret

stops.name: European Association of Zoos and Aquaria
Jewish Museum
stops.en: Jewish Historical Museum. History of the Jewish people, culture and religion.

stops.name: Het Scheepvaartmuseum
stops.en: Het Scheepvaartmuseum reopened in late 2011 following major renovations. Stimulating, interactive exhibitions allow visitors to explore 500 years of maritime history. The building, called the Arsenal, is impressive. The Central Square, the indoor courtyard can be visited for free and takes your breath away. Also the museum shop, the restaurant and the library are open to the public free of charge.

stops.name: Museum Willet-Holthuysen
stops.en: It is the only fully furnished canalside patrician house in Amsterdam that is open to the public. The museum has a large collection of silverware, plates, and books from the Dutch Golden Age. It also has a substantial collection of art.

stops.name: Micropia
stops.en: Museum about microbes.

stops.name: Dutch Resistance Museum
stops.en: Museum showing what Amsterdam and Holland were like during Nazi occupation. Has a very nice children's section. If you are visiting with kids and want to go to a museum about the Second World War in the Netherlands this is definitely recommended.

stops.name: Het Schip
stops.en: A museum about the Amsterdam School architectural style, housed in a building that is probably the city's best example of that style entrance.

stops.name: Diamond Museum Amsterdam
stops.en: This exhibition is about the history of the diamond trade in Amsterdam.

stops.name: Moco Museum
stops.en: Moco is a private museum of modern and contemporary art.

stops.name: Oosterpark
stops.en: Close to Plantage, this park holds several multicultural festivals throughout the year.

stops.name: Brouwersgracht
stops.en: This canal is sometimes cited as the "most beautiful street of Amsterdam". The name, "Brewer's Canal", refers to the many beer breweries along the canal in the 16th and 17th centuries. Nowadays, there's just one distillery left, De Ooievaar, that has been located here since 1782 and specializes in Dutch jenever and liquors. The warehouses here used to store goods such as coffee, spices and leather

stops.name: Westerpark
stops.en: A park at the western edge of the centre, with cultural activities in a former gas factory (Westergasfabriek). Access from Haarlemmerweg.

stops.name: Flevopark
stops.en: The Flevopark is in the Indische Buurt, at the eastern end of the Insulindeweg, next to the Jewish cemetery, the Flevoparkbad swimming pool, and the Nieuwe Diep inlet. There are two cafés open in spring/summer/autumn time and one festival each year.

stops.name: Pijpenkabinet & Smokiana
stops.en: Unique collection of smoking pipes in an authentic canal house from 1670. In the historic ambience of the collector's house, his collection of pipes covering 2,500 years is displayed. Visitors get a personal tour by enthusiast volunteers of the foundation that also runs the speciality shop in the basement: a huge selection of nearly 3,000 modern briar pipes are for sale, next to collectables and b

stops.name: Foam Fotografiemuseum Amsterdam
stops.en: Museum about photography. Group tours can be arranged via phone at +31 20 5516 505.

stops.name: Rembrandtpark
stops.en: Not too far west of the Vondelpark, but much quieter and larger in size.

stops.name: Wertheimpark
stops.en: A small park with a World War II memorial located at one of the nicest canals in Amsterdam.

stops.name: Royal Coster Diamonds
stops.en: This stately building is one of Amsterdam's two diamond factories. Guided tours are given showcasing the complicated diamond production process. It looks like just an ordinary jewellery shop, and of course it is, but there is a lot more to it. If you want to purchase diamonds, ask for the tax refund form so you can get up to 12% of the asking price back at the airport.

stops.name: Diemerpark
stops.en: This is a large park, a little like a dune park.

stops.name: Pianola museum
stops.en: A museum about Pianolas from the early 1900s. About a dozen are displayed at any one time, and every month a piano concert is held.

stops.name: Straat Museum
stops.en: Museum depicting street art in a large indoor exhibition.

stops.name: Orange Football Museum
stops.en: The legacy of Dutch football started in the 1970s, when Total Football, a revolutionary Dutch style of football, shook the world. The Netherlands is the best football nation that never won the World Cup: it lost the final three times, a national trauma. It did win the European Cup in 1988 lead by star player Marco van Basten. This museum has four floors dedicated to "Oranje", and a small cinema th

stops.name: Lomanstraat
stops.en: A charming photogenic street known for its curiously crooked trees, that form a kind of a tunnel.

stops.name: Allard Pierson Museum
stops.en: The Allard Pierson Museum is the archaeological museum of the University of Amsterdam. The ancient civilizations of Egypt, Cyprus, the Greek world, Etruria and the Roman Empire are revived in this museum. Art objects and utensils, dating from 4000 B.C. till 500 A.D. give a good impression of everyday life, mythology and religion in Antiquity.

stops.name: Civic Guards Gallery
stops.en: Just inside the arched gateway to the Amsterdam Museum is a hidden passageway with fifteen enormous 17th-century paintings; entrance is free to the public during museum hours. The collection features massive and meticulously realistic portraits of wealthy citizens from the Dutch Golden Age, the same class of subjects Rembrandt depicted in the most famous of Civic Guard paintings, the "Night Watch"

stops.name: Strandzuid
stops.en: With bar and restaurant

stops.name: Frans Hals
stops.en: Those interested in urban renewal may wish to visit Frans Hals, a 19th-century, residential area along the narrow Frans Halsstraat (straat means street). By 2019, the city had removed on-street parking and replaced it with greenery, benches, picnic tables and some playground equipment. There are several restaurants along the street.

stops.name: Lady Solid
stops.en: Lady Solid is a life-size statue of a woman in a striking pose standing with arms and feet spread. The statue has a water feature making the artwork controversial as it appears the lady has an incontinence problem. The pumping station features the artwork perhaps as it was "promoting the importance of well-functioning waterways", as suggested by a website on public art. The statue/fountain can be

stops.name: Amstelstation murals
stops.en: In the hall of Amstel railway station, there are several murals created in 1939 by Dutch artist Peter Alma, including a large mural at each end of the hall with a train motif.

stops.name: Floating houses
stops.en: There are two clusters of floating houses over a body of water. These small, modern houses are linked by a grid of walkways lined with railings holding life preservers and bicycles.

stops.name: OSCAM - Open Space Contemporary Art Museum
stops.en: OSCAM is the museological platform for art, fashion, design, craftsmanship and development in Amsterdam. It has a rich background in curating art, fashion and design exhibitions with a speciality in young (sub)cultures. By involving known and unknown creative talents in our exhibitions and programs, OSCAM inspires and fulfils the need for a connection platform with other social art institutes in A

stops.name: Koninklijk Paleis op de Dam
stops.lc: Het Paleis was oorspronkelijk het stadhuis van Amsterdam, maar is in langdurige bruikleen gegeven aan de Nederlandse Staat. Het wordt gebruikt voor officiële gelegenheden zoals staatsbezoeken etc. Indien er geen speciale dingen aan de hand zijn is het geopend voor publiek.

stops.name: Medieval Torture Museum
stops.lc: Het Medieval Torture Museum toont meer dan 100 martelwerktuigen die werden gebruikt in de Middeleeuwen.

stops.name: Van Goghmuseum
stops.lc: Museum is gevuld met werk van Vincent van Gogh, van zijn jonge jaren tot en met werk uit zijn laatste jaren. Museum organiseert regelmatig bijzondere (thema)tentoonstellingen over de schilders of de schilderkunst.

stops.name: Albert Cuyp Markt
stops.lc: De grootste dagelijkse markt van de stad.

eats.name: Gebr. Niemeijer
eats.note: French-style bakery with pastries, croissants, breads, sandwiches all baked fresh on premises. Open for breakfast and lunch, eat-in or takeaway. Bring the kids and eat in the small playroom upstairs.

eats.name: Van der Linde
eats.note: Its officially a bakery, but they don't sell bread. They do sell Amsterdam's most famous whipped ice cream, lovely almond cookies and cakes. The texture is really creamy and soft, it melts easily and

eats.name: Haring & Zo
eats.note: Serving for example fish sandwiches

eats.name: Rob Wigboldus Fishmonger
eats.note: Herring sandwiches for €3.50.

eats.name: Pasta Pasta
eats.note: Serves delicious pastas, made just as you want them. Choose a sauce, topping and pasta for a tasty, but well-priced meal.

eats.name: Julia's
eats.note: Italian cuisine, both eat-in and take-out; notable take-out item: Penne Bolognese with a tasty vegetarian sauce instead of a meat sauce.

eats.name: OCHA
eats.note: This used to be just the little "Thai snackbar around the corner", but since a raving review in the local newspaper Het Parool, big crowds are waiting in line to get seated during dinnertime. The scen

eats.name: Thaise Snackbar Bird
eats.note: Very crowded little snack bar with Thai food. Not to be confused with the restaurant of the same owner, on the other side of the street. Try the chicken in oyster sauce.

eats.name: New King
eats.note: Slowly becoming an institution, this hugely popular Mandarin Chinese restaurant seems to have found a perfect balance between food, price and ambiance. The food is authentically Chinese, delicious, fr

eats.name: Greetje
eats.note: Traditional Dutch, alongside French classics. Located in an historic building on a quiet side street near Central Station; it's off the beaten track so most of the diners are local. Open 6 days a week

eats.name: Kantjil & de Tijger
eats.note: Great spices and meat dishes, Indian/Indonesian food. Try the Nasi Goreng Rames.

eats.name: Rembrandt Corner
eats.note: Around the corner of the "Rembrandt Huis" is a very nice "Eetcafe" with fresh food, WiFi hot spots and internet workplaces. Try the dish of the day or the mussels.

eats.name: Tony's NY City Bagels
eats.note: Oversized cups of coffee, muffins and bagels. Muffins, brownies, giant cookies, cheesecake and bagels spread with various toppings are served at reasonable prices to a clientèle that is a mix of local

eats.name: Amsterdam Jewel Cruises
eats.note: À la carte dining while cruising the canals.

eats.name: Blue
eats.note: The selling point of this cafe is its 360 degrees view over Amsterdam. Its interior is minimalist and stylish. A great place to have a Dutch cup of coffee while taking in the views. Unfortunately, it'

eats.name: De Jaren
eats.note: A minimal art-deco interior next to Hotel d'Europe and a great view of where all the main canals come together (climb the stairs to the upper floor - the view is better and the crowds surprisingly thi

eats.name: Filter
eats.note: Small eco-friendly coffeebar situated in the lobby of hotel Ecomama. Serves great coffee, breakfast and a small selection of sweet and savoury treats. Also organic tea, juice and the best grilled-chee

eats.name: The Grasshopper
eats.note: On the edge of the Red Light District, has an upper-floor bar.

eats.name: Hannekes Boom
eats.note: One of Amsterdam's hidden secrets, Hannekes Boom is a cosy, somewhat ramshackle, bar with a waterfront along the IJ. It's a great place to just hang out and have a beer. Not for clubbers, but for thos

eats.name: Brouwerij de Prael
eats.note: A brewery, tasting room and beer shop all in one.

eats.name: Cracked Kettle
eats.note: This beer, wine, and spirits shop carries independent, unique, and rare bottles. The staff are friendly, but the space is quite confined and obtaining bottles from the very top shelves requires assist

eats.name: De Bierkoning
eats.note: Not a café, but a 'supermarket' specialized in beer. It has over a thousand beers, about half of it Dutch.

eats.name: In De Wildeman
eats.note: A very well stocked beer café, or actually beer tasting room (bierproeflokaal) in the centre of the inner city. 17 beers (usually from various countries) and a cider on draught, and about 250 differen

eats.name: Wynand Fockink
eats.note: Wynand Fockink is a distillery that started in 1679. They offer distillery tours, but you must reserve at least a week in advance as they fill up quickly. It is also a tasting room and a liquor store.

eats.name: Belgique
eats.note: One of the smallest bars in Amsterdam, there is seating for at most 15 people. Specialising in Belgian beers, extensive menu that includes some hard to find beers on tap. This place is smoke friendly

eats.name: Cuba
eats.note: Great bar, really nice atmosphere, close to the Red Light District with a nice terrace in the summer. Selection of cheap cocktails and long island ice tea.

eats.name: Gollem
eats.note: A special beer café, serving many beers, especially from Belgium, Germany, Czech Republic and other countries.

eats.name: Katoen
eats.note: Close to the southern part of the Canal District. Alternative music and cosy atmosphere also in the evenings.

eats.name: Molly Malones Irish Pub
eats.note: Authentic Irish pub with food. Mix of expatriates, locals and tourists, friendly staff, on a canal off the Zeedijk, close to Centraal Station and Warmoesstraat. Open every night, live music in the wee

eats.name: Schuim
eats.note: The super comfy cafe is a great place to spend entire rainy days at a time. It heats up quite a bit at night. Pot smoking seems to be tolerated even though Schuim is definitely not a "coffeeshop".

eats.name: Speijk
eats.note: Awesome bar with lost of fun, artsy crazy locals. Various DJ play different styles. Open till late in the morning. Best place to meet laid-back and awesome Amsterdammers!!

eats.name: Irish Pub Slainte
eats.note: An Irish pub that also serves very inexpensive food like cheese sandwiches. Everything you can expect from an Irish pub nearby the Oude Kerk and nearby the Red Light District.

eats.name: Bitterzoet
eats.note: This placed used to be alternative, but changed ownership and is now more hip hop and R&B oriented. Check their agenda to see what they're doing.

eats.name: Winston Kingdom
eats.note: Music venue and nightclub in the red light district.

eats.name: 420CAFE
eats.note: Known for their moderate prices. The music played here is Classic Rock & Frank Zappa.

eats.name: Bluebird
eats.note: One of the best selections of pot in Amsterdam.

eats.name: De Dampkring
eats.note: The shop was featured in a scene in Ocean's Twelve. Very decent hashish ("Rifman" products), rather high prices. Has won the Cannabis Cup numerous times.

eats.name: Green House
eats.note: Usually pretty crowded but when warm or if you can get a seat definitely one of the nice coffeeshops near the Red Light District. Also has a bar next door.

eats.name: Hill Street Blues
eats.note: Lively atmosphere but buy cannabis elsewhere.

eats.name: Kadinsky
eats.note: It looks completely different from before, and now has three floors with a slick minimalist design.A great place to smoke your goods, and actually serves a good cup of coffee too.

eats.name: Pancakes! Amsterdam
eats.note: Amazing variety of both sweet and savory pancakes. The quaint atmosphere and the street side tables are great for watching people. The only downfall is that street-side tables attract too many tourist

eats.name: The Pancake Bakery
eats.note: Large selection of sweet or savory pancakes.

eats.name: Frens Haringhandel
eats.note: A stall offering simple Dutch seafood fare like Kibbling (fried fish) and Haring (raw herring).

eats.name: De Blauwe Hollander
eats.note: Dutch restaurant with an extensive menu of hearty home-cooked dishes like herrings, pea soup and hutspot. Unlike most restaurants in this area, this one gets local diners too, and if it gets crowded e

eats.name: Damsteeg
eats.note: They specialise in fish dishes, but they also have a wide variety of meat and vegetarian meals to choose from. With bar.

eats.name: Letting
eats.note: Indian-owned breakfast, brunch and lunch spot. Letting offers a range of soups, sandwiches and scones, and it's on a street which is packed with an ever-changing line-up of fun boutiques.

eats.name: Holtkamp
eats.note: Best pastry cafe in Amsterdam. Much better than the Zeitan, which many recommend. Do try the "holdkampf" with fillings! The Sachertorte is famous as a favorite of the former Queen Beatrix.

eats.name: Alberto's Steakhouse
eats.note: Uruguayan Steakhouse with well-grilled steaks

eats.name: Akbar
eats.note: Indian restaurant, Muslim (halal) / Hindu (no beef). Good quality dishes from different regions of India.

eats.name: La Margarita
eats.note: This Caribbean restaurant offers a huge range of plates, including three different vegetarian options. Every dish comes with ample sides of white rice, black beans, plantains, and vegetables. In addit

eats.name: 't Arendsnest
eats.note: Excellent biercafe serving only Dutch beers and liqueurs, including jenever. Around 30 beers on tap, 17 or so which change regularly, and over 100 bottled. Very friendly bartenders who know beer well

eats.name: Dan Murphy's
eats.note: One of the many Irish pubs in the city. People from all over the world meet here and watch football, rugby and typical Irish sports like hurling and Gaelic football while drinking a pint of Guinness.

eats.name: Feijoa
eats.note: Cocktail bar with a lovely atmosphere, pleasant music and friendly staff, including one of the Netherlands leading cocktail barmen. Will make any cocktail you ask for.

eats.name: Hard Rock Cafe
eats.note: This is close to, or right next to the Holland Casino also close to the Leidseplein. Great service, great food, and plenty of drinks.

eats.name: Mulligans Irish Music Bar
eats.note: The oldest Irish bar in Amsterdam, Mulligans has live music most nights. This is where the traditional music crowd gathers.

eats.name: l'Opera
eats.note: A friendly spot for coffee, a beer, or something stronger. You may at first only notice the outside seating and the enclosed terrace, but there is also an elegant, (usually) quieter indoor area. Food,

eats.name: Whisky Cafe L&B
eats.note: If you like whisky, this small, laid-back and friendly cafe is the ideal place to visit. Many unusual whiskies from independent bottlers and closed distilleries are available. The menu stretches along

eats.name: Chicago Social Club
eats.note: Amsterdam's nightlife king Casper Reinders joined with the founders of Bitterzoet and the owners of Boom Chicago to bring quality clubbing to the Leidspelein.

eats.name: Escape
eats.note: A large, fairly uninspiring nightclub that mostly plays mainstream house music. The first hall is large and attracts the more or less wannabe hip people of the city, although the crowd is diverse. The

eats.name: Jimmy Woo
eats.note: The most glamorous club in Amsterdam offers a selection of house and R&B, with a spectacularly lit dance floor downstairs. It is relatively small and there is table service, so it feels a bit like a V

eats.name: Melkweg
eats.note: A former milk factory, now it's one of the best live venues in Amsterdam. Its interior is not as good as Paradiso, but it feels more like a nightclub as the music is dance/trance-oriented. Popular amo

eats.name: Paradiso
eats.note: Sometimes referred to as a nightclub, it feels more like a nightly music venue and is the safest bet in town. Its interior is phenomenal as it is housed in a former church, but the main room has relat

eats.name: Studio 80
eats.note: This is a somewhat more underground, intimate club that's easy to miss because of its flashy neighbours. It prides itself on trying to stay at the forefront of electronic music in the city.

eats.name: Sugar Factory
eats.note: Bit of a remarkable place that integrates art, music, culture, theatre and nightclub into one. It has a relaxed atmosphere with an eccentric, artistic audience.

eats.name: The Cave Rockclub
eats.note: Cozy metal bar with friendly bar staff and interesting regulars, with live performances by touring metal bands on weekends.

eats.name: Waterhole
eats.note: Light rock/funk jam sessions in a dingy but atmospheric bar with pooltables. Live bands play every night of the week.

eats.name: Betty Too
eats.note: Absolute gem, cozy and friendly place with moderate prizes and interesting, international crowd.

eats.name: Bulldog
eats.note: This is the original shop that used to be a police department. Now it turned into a chain of touristy coffeeshops, bars, hotels and even an energy drink.

eats.name: Global Chillage
eats.note: Good produce and nice tunes but uncomfortable seating.

eats.name: Grey Area
eats.note: Tiny, but famous for their outstanding weed, especially "American" strains.

eats.name: The Otherside
eats.note: Gay coffeeshop.

eats.name: Burgermeester
eats.note: Yes, they serve burgers here. But don't expect a McDonalds wannabe. They are quality meat, fish or vegetarian burgers. The place is so popular that they opened 2 more branches in the city. Great if yo

eats.name: Kinnaree
eats.note: Amazing Thai food. Good atmosphere, good service despite being quite busy, but the food is why you would come here. Highly recommended.

eats.name: Long Pura
eats.note: Indonesian food, try the rice table.

eats.name: Proeverij 274
eats.note: Small, cosy restaurant at one of the main canals. Business but also romantic dinner. Small menu, new Dutch cuisine with classic French influences. The menu features mainly organic regional produce. Pe

eats.name: Maloe Melo
eats.note: Small blues bar which is separated in two parts: a free part in the front, €5 entrance fee in the back where blues or rock 'n' roll bands play live every night of the week.

eats.name: 't Smalle
eats.note: Some say this place has the most beautiful terrace in Amsterdam. It's not big but you sit right beside the canal. And if it's too cold to sit outside check out the beautifully restored interior in thi

eats.name: Cafe P 96
eats.note: Great character at this pub, lovely outdoor terrace on a houseboat makes for a nice evening or afternoon. Good selection of Dutch and Belgian beers.

eats.name: Soundgarden
eats.note: Top metal/grungy/punky pub, most relaxed drinking atmosphere in town. Really nice, secluded terrace for drinking beer in the sun. can smoke, but not buy, puff.

eats.name: Bar Brandstof
eats.note: Relatively new bar with a big and often busy terrace. Gets absolutely crowded on Friday after work hours

eats.name: Bar Struik
eats.note: Hangout for the urban 20 and 30-somethings. Every day except Friday they serve 1 dish for . Gets really crowded in the weekends.

eats.name: Cafe Chaos
eats.note: Typical Amsterdam brown bar. Throw your peanuts shells on the floor while looking at the furniture.

eats.name: Barney's
eats.note: Coffeeshop.

eats.name: Coffeeshop Ibiza
eats.note: Big coffee shop.

eats.name: Cafe Kadijk
eats.note: Cafe Kadijk is a small Indonesian restaurant that offers good food at a decent price. The restaurant has a coffee shop vibe and is located in a "trendy" area. Just outside Amsterdam's city centre, it

eats.name: De plantage
eats.note: Big restaurant with a nice terrace in the summer, open all day with breakfast, lunch and dinner.

eats.name: Restaurant Plancius
eats.note: Has a nice high tea.

eats.name: Tempura
eats.note: Nice Japanese restaurant, with a very lovely guest woman.

eats.name: De Pizzabakkers
eats.note: Hip pizza restaurant, with good stone-baked pizzas. Suitable for children. Almost always busy, so reservation is recommended.

eats.name: Aguada
eats.note: Indian and Indonesian influenced. Cosy restaurant. The rendang is a little too sweet but the thali is excellent.

eats.name: Brouwerij 't IJ
eats.note: Its label with an ostrich egg is a visual pun, as IJ and 'ei' - the word for egg - sound the same in Dutch. East of the centre, close to Artis Zoo, in a former bath house beside a windmill. A small-sc

eats.name: Café Smit & Voogt
eats.note: Locals love this place. It is situated inside a beautiful building and has timber booths and seating inside . There is also seating on the footpath which is well placed to catch the afternoon sun. Ser

eats.name: Albina
eats.note: It's cheap and very good. If you arrive around dinnertime you probably have to wait for a table. The surroundings are depressing but the food is so good you will come back anyway.

eats.name: Tjin's Gelderlandplein
eats.note: Tasty, great value Surinamese take-out. Sandwiches. Located a short walk from the Zuidas area hotels. A few tables are also available to eat in.

eats.name: CTaste
eats.note: Dining in the dark. All waiters are blind, and serve you dinner in a completely dark restaurant. A very weird, but actually quite fun experience.

eats.name: OCCII
eats.note: A rock venue for cutting-edge music (punk, noise, riot grrrl, etc.)

eats.name: Club Media
eats.note: Completely organic menu, fair selection, good prices, lovely staff, free fruit!

eats.name: Katsu
eats.note: Just around the corner from Media, good prices + nice atmosphere.

eats.name: 't Blauwe Theehuis
eats.note: Basic bar and beer garden

eats.name: De Roos
eats.note: Quite tea house with a small garden.

eats.name: Dosa
eats.note: They specialise in traditional Southern Indian cuisine, especially the eponymous 'Dosa' (a rice and lentil pancake with a variety of fillings). The food is outstanding and well worth hunting out. The

eats.name: Foodhallen
eats.note: International food court with 20 food-stands housed in a large building that was once a tram depot.

eats.name: Hap Hmm
eats.note: Traditional Dutch cuisine. The restaurant may be cramped, but it does serve some quality and rustic Dutch fare. This place is cash only.

eats.name: Sora Sapporo Ramen - West
eats.note: Small ramen restaurant with friendly staff, quick service, and good selection of ramen & appetizers. Also serve beer & sake. Closes early and small seating so might want to reserve on weekends.

eats.name: TonTon Club West
eats.note: TonTon Club is an excellent place for a good night out. The place has a unique atmosphere with Japan as its inspiration. Upstairs there are arcades and button bashers, downstairs there's room for drin

eats.name: Cafe L'Affice
eats.note: Small bar with friendly staff and a cosy and candle-lit atmosphere. Selection of beers on tap and in bottles, including a triple blonde specially made for the bar. Small selection of bar food as well.

eats.name: Café Modern B.V.
eats.note: A restaurant and cafe in a hall which used to be a bank.

eats.name: Café-restaurant Stork
eats.note: A fish and seafood restaurant in an old factory on the banks of the river.

eats.name: Hangar Amsterdam
eats.note: A redesigned aircraft hangar, turned restaurant.

eats.name: Mount Everest Tandoori
eats.note: An Indian and Nepalese restaurant. Vegetarian friendly.

eats.name: Pllek
eats.note: A bar and restaurant in an old industrial area, by the river.

eats.name: Boerenjongens Eetwinkel
eats.note: A deli shop annex lunch room with products from the region.

eats.name: IJsburg
eats.note: Ice cream shop.

eats.name: Biertuin
eats.note: Oktoberfest-style biergarten, so expect long tables and a wide variety of bottled beers available. It has a nice atmosphere during warm summer evenings. Try the Hamburger Deluxe or chicken menus. And

eats.name: Bloem op IJburg
eats.note: Italian restaurant.

eats.name: Silk Road Restaurant
eats.note: Eastern and Western fusion meals with both à la carte and (on highly occupied days o­nly) a live cooking theme buffet. The restaurant has a view of the river IJ. Open 7 days per week for lunch and din

eats.name: Espressofabriek
eats.note: Coffee bar.

eats.name: N.A.P.
eats.note: A harbour-side cafe and restaurant with a view of the marina. You can just stop by for a cup of coffee, have breakfast, lunch or dinner. Stylish interior.

eats.name: Delirium Café Amsterdam
eats.note: With over 500 bottled beers and 20 craft beers on draft, the biggest craft beer bar in Amsterdam.

eats.name: Panama
eats.note: This nightclub is relatively close to the city centre. It has its fair share of nice nights and the view on the water is excellent.

eats.name: Canvas
eats.note: A restaurant-bar-club, this urban and edgy den in a former newspaper office is a great place to go out at night. With nice views of the city and a varied music repertoire (alternative, jazz, funk), it

eats.name: Kam Yin Chinees Surinaams restaurant
eats.note: Surinamese and Indonesian cuisine. Very good Moksi Meti (marinated pork and sausages with noodles). Popular with the locals. Take-away.

eats.name: Lebkov & Sons
eats.note: Sandwich bar. Mainly caters to office workers in surrounding buildings. Try the hummus & sun-dried tomato.

eats.name: Lomnava Kenkey House
eats.note: One of the few Ghanaian snack bars in Amsterdam. Specializes in Kenkey (a sort of sourdough dumpling), but has a wide range of West-African cuisine at very reasonable prices.

eats.name: Marmaris Grill & Pizza
eats.note: Relatively up-market Turkish/Mediterranean restaurant in the fancy new building opposite station Bijlmer-Arena. Great food, presentation and service - definitely worth the price. On cold days, avoid s

eats.name: Oma Ietje
eats.note: Inevitably, hipsters have even found their way into the Bijlmer. Part-funded by crowdfunding. Very worthy 'Swedish style' coffee house. Coffee, biological lemonade and cakes. Also showcases art by loc

eats.name: Elixer
eats.note: Restaurant dedicated to circular economy. Occupies a formerly derelict building, all furnishings are second-hand, and as much food as possible is home-grown or locally sourced. Profits are invested in

eats.name: Yemayá’s Vegan Corner
eats.note: Surinamese Caribbean vegan food made by a local collective. Also delivers within Zuidoost and Diemen.

eats.name: De Proefzaak
eats.note: In 2015 the first monastery - the Kleiklooster - opened in the Bijlmer, and as good monks do, they started brewing beer. Good beer, if somewhat eccentric. This is their tasting hall where you can samp

eats.name: Brasserie Hoekenrode
eats.note: Large cafe under the Hampton/Hilton hotel. During the day mainly caters to the nearby office crowd, but in the evenings it gets more local.

eats.name: Roots
eats.note: First - and as of September 2021, only - coffee shop in Zuidoost. Caters to locals, day trippers to large venues nearby and tourists in the surrounding hotels. Take-away or smoke in.

eats.name: Bordewijk
eats.note: Al jaren een favoriet van Johannes van Dam. Eerlijke, Franse keuken waar de gerechten worden bereid met verse ingrediënten en zonder al te veel opsmuk. Reserveren wordt op prijs gesteld.

eats.name: Dok 48
eats.note: Café restaurant Dok 48 heeft een groot terras direct aan het water en uitzicht op de sluis.
